newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices weaken but stave off big falls.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices weaken but stave off big falls.

text.p: Oil prices edged lower on technical weakness on Friday, but traders and analysts said the market could probably stave off a repeat of last week's slide which threatened to send crude markets into a lengthy downward spiral.
London futures for bellwether Brent blend closed 16 cents lower at $22.26 after a flurry of last-minute selling when the price fell below the $22.30 level.

"The market's still in the doldrums," said one trader. "But at least it's braked last week's fall." Last week key Brent futures shed $1.30, this week they lost just 29 cents against last Friday's close.
Prices found support earlier this week after U.S. government and industry figures showed a pause in the growth of inventories back towards normal levels from last year's record lows.
U.S. distillate stocks, including heating oil, fell by 4.8 million barrels last week and crude stocks fell by 1.5 million.
Historically low stocks have haunted the market over the last year -- a result of oil companies' policy of running down inventory to shave costs.
That has left prices vulnerable to short-term weather shocks or supply disruption, which boosted the market to a six-year high of $25 for Brent hit in October.
But U.S. inventories are now running closer to year-ago levels and many are looking ahead to the end of winter and the heating oil season.
Weather forecasts for the weekend were for higher than normal temperatures for the time of year for both the key U.S. northeast and northwest European heating oil regions.
That helped undermine European gas oil prices which slumped $8 in London to $200 a tonne, hitting hard refinery profit margins.
Lower demand for oil products in northern Asia, also undercut by mild weather, prompted reduced refinery operations throughout the region.
